questions.q: Find the area of a quadrilateral ABCD whose area is twice the area of a triangle PQR. The sides of triangle PQR are in the ratio 4:5:6 and the perimeter of the triangle is 90 cm (use $\sqrt{7} = 2.6$).
questions.solution:
Sides = 24, 30, 36 cm (ratio 4:5:6, perimeter 90). Semi-perimeter s = 45, so by Heron's formula area = $\sqrt{45 \times 21 \times 15 \times 9} = 135\sqrt{7} = 135 \times 2.6 = 351$ cm². Quadrilateral = 2 × 351 = 702 cm².
**Answer: 702 cm2**

questions.q: 20% of a number is more than 20% of 620 by 210. The number is:

Anand has ₹1407 with him. He divides this amount between his two sons, Anil and Ashok, and asks them to invest their respective shares at a compound interest rate of 10% per annum, compounded annually. It is observed that Anil’s investment amounts to the same value after 15 years as Ashok’s investment does after 16 years. How much (in ₹) did Anand give to Ashok?
questions.solution:
Anil's money for 15 years equals Ashok's money for 16 years, so Anil's share × 1.1^15 = Ashok's share × 1.1^16, giving Anil : Ashok = 1.1 : 1 = 11 : 10. Ashok's part = 10/21 × 1407 = 670.
**Answer: 670**
questions.shortcut: Equal final amounts means the shares differ by exactly one year of growth (factor 1.1).

questions.q: The average of 13 numbers is 8. If each number is multiplied by 7, then what will the new average be:
questions.solution:
Multiplying every number by 7 multiplies the average by 7: 8 × 7 = 56.
**Answer: 56**

questions.q: Girish scored 572 marks in an examination and was 30 marks short of 28% of maximum marks. In the same examination, his friend scored 473 marks. What is the percentage of marks scored by his friend?
questions.solution:
572 + 30 = 602 is 28% of the maximum marks, so maximum = 2150. The friend's 473 is 473/2150 = 22%.
**Answer: 22%**

questions.q: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 38 hours respectively. A third tap can empty it in 38 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
questions.solution:
The two filling taps give 1/4 + 1/38 per hour and the emptying tap removes 1/38, so the net rate is 1/4 per hour: the full cistern takes 4 hours and one-fourth takes 1 hour.
**Answer: 1**
questions.shortcut: The 38-hour fill and 38-hour drain cancel exactly.

questions.q: If the median of a data is 61.54 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use the empirical formula to find the answer)
questions.solution:
Empirical formula: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, so Mode − Median = 2(Median − Mean). Hence Median − Mean = 61.54 / 2 = 30.77.
**Answer: 30.77**

questions.q: A train travelling at 60 km/hr crosses another train travelling in the opposite direction at 84 km/hr in 30 seconds. What is the combined length (in m) of both the trains?
questions.solution:
Opposite directions: relative speed = 60 + 84 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s. Combined length = 40 × 30 = 1200 m.
**Answer: 1200**

questions.q: A tower stands vertically on the ground. From a point on the ground which is 28.6 m away from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be 45°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
At 45° the height equals the horizontal distance, so the tower is 28.6 m tall.
**Answer: 28.6 m**

questions.q: What is the maximum value that must be assigned to A so that the 8-digit number 816A0408 is divisible by 4?
questions.solution:
A number is divisible by 4 when its last two digits form a multiple of 4. Here the last two digits are 08, which works for any A, so the greatest digit that can be assigned is 9.
**Answer: 9**

questions.q: Three friends X, Y and Z started a business by investing a sum of money in the ratio of 4 : 2 : 5. After 6 months, X withdraws half of his capital. If the sum invested by Z is ₹23,000, then out of a total annual profit of ₹37,000, what is the difference between X's and Y's profit?
questions.solution:
Capitals are X 18400, Y 9200, Z 23000. X's capital for the year works out to 18400 × 6 + 9200 × 6 = 165600 unit-months, Y's is 9200 × 12 = 110400 and Z's is 23000 × 12 = 276000. Ratio = 3 : 2 : 5. Profit shares of X and Y are 11100 and 7400, so the difference is 3700.
**Answer: ₹3700**
questions.shortcut: Reduce the three products by their common factor to get 3 : 2 : 5.

questions.q: At present, Sharad is three times as old as his son, and his daughter is 3 years younger than the son. If the sum of the ages of these three people 3 years ago was 63 years, then Sharad's present age (in years) is:
questions.solution:
Let the son be s. Sharad is 3s and the daughter is s − 3. Three years ago their ages were 3s − 3, s − 3 and s − 6, totalling 5s − 12 = 63, so s = 15. Sharad is 45.
**Answer: 45**

questions.q: Find the area of a regular hexagon whose side measures 14√3 cm.
questions.solution:
Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3/2)a². With a = 14√3, a² = 588, so area = (3√3/2) × 588 = 882√3 cm².
**Answer: 882√3 cm2**

questions.q: If both the roots of the quadratic equation A(8x 2 + 4) + Bx + 4x 2 − 8 = 0 and 3A(2x 2 + 1) + Kx + 3x 2 − 6 = 0 are common, then what is the value of 9B 2 − 16K 2 ?
questions.solution:
Expanding, the first equation is (8A+4)x² + Bx + (4A−8) = 0 and the second is (6A+3)x² + Kx + (3A−6) = 0. Their x² and constant coefficients are in the ratio 3 : 4 each, so for the same two roots the x-coefficients must also be in that ratio: K = 3B/4. Then 16K² = 9B², so 9B² − 16K² = 0.
**Answer: 0**

questions.q: In a triangle PQR, ∠ QOR = 130°, where O is the in-centre of triangle PQR. The measure of ∠ QPR is:
questions.solution:
For the in-centre O, ∠QOR = 90° + ∠P/2. So 130° = 90° + ∠P/2, giving ∠QPR = 80°.
**Answer: 80°**

questions.q: Three printing machines, P, Q and R, when each is working alone, can print one lakh books in, respectively, 8 hours, 16 hours and 24 hours. These machines print books in turns of one hour each, starting with P, followed by Q and then by R. However, after a total of 9 hours, P stops functioning, but Q and R continue working alternately for an hour each, with Q working during the 10th hour, till the printing of all the one lakh books is completed. In how many hours in all did machines Q and R complete printing the remaining books?
questions.solution:
Per lakh, P does 1/8, Q 1/16, R 1/24 per hour. One P-Q-R round of 3 hours = 11/48, so 9 hours = 33/48. Remaining = 15/48. Q and R alternating give 1/16 + 1/24 = 5/48 per two hours, so 3 pairs = 6 hours.
**Answer: 6**

questions.q: At what rate (in percentage) per year will a sum of money double itself in 16 years on simple interest?
questions.solution:
To double the money, SI = principal, so P × R × 16/100 = P, which gives R = 100/16 = 6.25%.
**Answer: 6.25**

questions.q: There are 78 members in group A, 22 members in group B and 34 members in group C. All the members of these groups went to a restaurant. The average amounts spent on each member of groups A, B and C are ₹136, ₹383 and ₹457, respectively. The overall average amount (in ₹) spent per member is:
P sells an item to Q at 50% profit. Q sells the same item to R at 60% loss. If R paid ₹ 3234 for the item, then at what price (in ₹) is the item purchased by P?
questions.solution:
R paid 3234, which is 40% of Q's cost (60% loss), so Q's cost = 8085. That was P's selling price at 50% profit, so P's cost = 8085 / 1.5 = 5390.
**Answer: 5390**

questions.q: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹500 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 50% and 28% and still earns ₹958 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 77%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.solution:
On X: marked price × 0.5 × 0.72 = 500 + 958 = 1458, so the marked price is 4050. On Y with 77% discount the selling price is 23% of 4050 = 931.50. Profit = 431.50 on cost 500 = 86.3%.
**Answer: 86.3%**

questions.q: Find the third proportional to the numbers 16 and 24.
questions.solution:
The third proportional to a and b is b²/a = 24²/16 = 36.
**Answer: 36**
